    This year, 2024, is 41 years since N. Robin Crossby            N. Robin Crossby’s exemplary and most enduring
    released the first Hârn product in 1983, and 38 years          contribution to the hobby of tabletop roleplaying is his map
    since HârnMaster was released in 1986 to provide rules to      of the island of Hârn. From its crayon-rendered inception
    support the setting. A huge range of materials has been        to his culminating multilayered PDF and definitive hard
    developed both for the island of Hârn and its various          copy version of 2010, this image—alone—best evokes what
    realms and peoples, as well as for regions far beyond that     most fans have come to love about gaming in Crossby’s
    misty island’s shores.                                         world: its consistency and detail.
        The magic of Robin’s work has at least partly been found       While much of the HârnWorld setting was in print
    in the balance between real world sensibilities and the        three years before the HârnMaster system, the two
    wonder of medieval fantasy. For generations, his world         have ultimately been linked for the greater part of their
    has provided a foundation and springboard to imaginative       publishing lives, just like almost every other successful
    gaming that seems plausible, with GMs and players              RPG. Over recent years, the setting and the system have
    discovering as much as they create. The HârnMaster rules       drifted slightly apart, perhaps by design, perhaps even
    likewise present mechanisms that are based on common           celebrated by some. However, such division has led in part
    sense—they describe and simulate how things work on            to an unfortunate isolation that, while leaving die-hards
    Kethira rather than force how things work on Kethira to fit    nearly unaffected, often confuses curious new gamers,
    a game.                                                        even to the point of their wondering if Hârn publications
        A few years back we asked Walt to join us, to build upon   are created with actual play in mind.
    this legacy and to create a new edition that updates the           The primary intention, then, of HârnMaster:
    previous work. We’ve kept the core mechanics, explored         Roleplaying in the World of Kèthîra (HMK) is to
    some unaddressed corners, and smoothed out the                 reunite more clearly Crossby’s world with an updated and
    occasional rough edge, all with an eye towards the world as    expanded version of his rules—indeed, to publish with
    Robin dreamed it up.                                           actual play in mind. Given the literally millions of words
                                                                   already written about its cultures and peoples, Kethira
    Cheers and Happy Explorations.                                 does not lack for descriptive richness. This substantial
                                                                   body of work can be an advantage to new gamers—there
    Jeremy Baker and Ken Snellings                                 is a great deal of quality material immediately available
    Keléstia Productions                                           to embrace. On the other hand, this very amount can also
                                                                   make it difficult to know: where does one start?
                                                                       Thus, HMK’s second, equally important, intention is to
                                                                   be just such an overt launch point. Its 436 pages provide
                                                                   mechanics for making characters, testing their skills
                                                                   and abilities, and ushering them through adventures
                                                                   involving intrigue, action, profound mysteries, and strange
                                                                   creatures and entities. It is a complete fantasy roleplaying
                                                                   game, gathered in one clear place.
                                                                       But to make gaming in Kethira easier for both veteran
                                                                   and new players, more will be needed. The hobby is
                                                                   driven by committed players and, especially, hardworking
                                                                   gamemasters. There are few of either who do not tinker
                                                                   with a game’s canonised setting and rules to fit their own
                                                                   vision. However, there have been few RPGs over the years
                                                                   that have forced them to do so the way Hârn’s sometimes
                                                                   confusing level of entry has required.
                                                                       Keléstia Productions will continue to expand the setting
                                                                   with the celebrated consistency and detail, while also
                                                                   anchoring it clearly to the system Crossby himself tailored
                                                                   to express its reality. The release of HMK also coincides
                                                                   with a new commitment to adventure—starting with a free
                                                                   quickstart download, but soon to include a fuller campaign
                                                                   with a GM screen and kit. Our third intention, therefore,
                                                                   is to make running games on Kethira using HârnMaster
                                                                   easier. This rulebook is just the beginning.

chapter 1

Hârn
and the World of Kèthîra
          he takes the last step off the gangway
          in a short leap, thankful to be back on
          solid ground. Three days to sail the swift
Emel Straits was not a long time, but ten years
since having been on a ship will leave her feeling
the swells for a while. After a quick nod of thanks
to the captain up on deck, Nolora turns to find
herself suddenly impeded by a swarm of milling
sailors along the wharf.
   Memories return of the brief journey in her
youth to this same Cherafir port—the web of thick
cordage, the din of shouts and conversation in a
dozen tongues, the wide-ranging canvas of folk
from all realms of Venarive. Jostled backwards
by the crowd further onto the pier, Nolora finally
sees what the throng is: the boarding crew of the
immense three-masted merchant galley berthed
opposite the vessel she just left. Secured stern
first to the wharf, the Larumar’s length juts over
a hundred feet into the water beyond, where
mooring lines from a handful of small oared boats
steady its prow for the anticipated row out to sea.
   Nolora grips her thick bow stave for leverage in
making headway ashore through the embarking
sailors. While not menacing, they part absently,
Nolora not hesitating to lend a subtle elbow to her
progress. She pauses at hearing a greeting called
out in her native Emelan. Ahead, emerging out
of the crowd, appears Elben, robed now in finer
silk and leather than she recalls from before, the
corners of his eyes more creased, the hair at his
temples more greyed. He repeats her name while
extending a hand, and says: ‘Welcome back to the
Misty Isle!—­it’s been far too long.’

chapter 2

Character
         ost natives of venarive assume that
         the future will look very much like the
         past. Rivers may change their course,
cities wax and wane and turn to dust, but the
things that follow will be mostly like the things
that came before. Thus, there is little thought given
to changing the world. Scholars do not expect to
revolutionise their fields, warlords look to one
conquest at a time—save for the occasional effort
to restore a long-lost empire. There is tremendous
respect, even veneration, for past masters. Those
people looking for power—whether arcane,
economic, or political—expect to find it only in the
framework provided by their predecessors.



However, there is one type of person whose
ambitions are not bound by convention, who
believes that revolutionary change is possible,
and who believes that they succeed or fail based
on their own capabilities and not the morality of
their actions or their relationship to their god.
These men and women are condemned by their
mental defects to live outside normal society—in
fact, to be constantly engaged in dangerous and
often violent action. While they might find brief
respite at times, and even achieve some temporary
social status, they are driven by demons that keep
them from long enjoying such times of rest. They
are called adventurers, and they are a rude and
unreasonable kind.

Elder Folk Age
The ageing of each Elder Folk may require particular age group rules.
Ænarin: Half-elf PCs select or roll for age as for humans. While Ænarin
age like humans throughout most of their lives, they extend the old
group by 20 years, ultimately living a few decades beyond 100.
Malákta: although they generally age as for humans, all Malakta PCs are
by default in the young group. Of the scant hundred known to exist on
Kethira, only a few leaders are mature (and none are old).
Nâdi: select or roll for age as for humans.
Kúzhai: despite living 200–300 years, the Kuzhai usually send forth only
seasoned kin to mingle in human affairs. Thus, all Kuzhai PCs belong to
the mature group, with an actual age of around 75–125 years.
Sinái and Sidhé: while elven folk do not die of natural causes, all Ælrhin
PCs begin the campaign in the young group, during the first or second
century of their lives. They often ceremoniously embark on adventure
when 144 years old, the ‘age of maturity’.

Background
After establishing Parent Occupation for characters, determine their
family’s Background—whether they resided in a sizeable settlement
or in the countryside. There are four possible Backgrounds: Urban,
City, Rural, or Wilderness. Each provides special opportunities for skill
development in step 12.

  8 Make d100 Background Roll.

Make a d100 roll against the Urban chance corresponding to the Parent
Occupation determined in step 7, unless the character is from a non-
Settled Tribal Society. If the result is less than or equal to this number,
the character has an Urban background; otherwise, the character has a
Rural background. Even if the Urban chance is a o or 100, make the d100
roll anyway—see the City and Wilderness rules, below, and the examples
in the sidebar.

Urban Background
All Urban settlements are measured according to their Market Size
(MKT), a reflection of population, proximity to trade routes, and
surrounding geography. Listed are some notable examples.

Persona
While Birth information gives a broad cultural context
(steps 1–5), and Family characteristics help explain
parental and clan influence (steps 6–9), Persona describes
                                                                a




a character’s individual aptitude and unique development.           character traits
It is largely defined through the following five elements.          In addition to the various numerical ratings,
                                                                    characters possess qualitative descriptions called
Characteristics: characters have six physical and six               Traits, applicable to both physique and personality.
mental Attributes that measure the innate talent of their           These can be assigned during character generation
body and mind. There are other characteristics to reflect           (Sunsign and Morality Traits); acquired during game
morality and inherent psychic ability.                              play (a limp resulting from injury); suffered as mental
                                                                    trauma (paranoid); or simply created whole-cloth
Occupation: characters select an occupation, either the             (devoted to avenging a sibling’s death).
same as their parents or a different one. They are usually             Character traits are often not quantified. They
restricted to those that appear on their society’s Class &          remain narrative details the player expresses through
Occupation table of a social class no higher than their             roleplaying to whatever extent they wish. Psyche traits
parents’. The GM might allow exceptions for a unique                can also develop into more intense conditions called
backstory, or level even further restrictions, such as              impulses or disorders—these can be acquired during
requiring a strong Aura to enter esoteric occupations.              character generation (page 40) or as the campaign
                                                                    unfolds (page 188).
Skills: the several dozen skills in the game measure a                 How many total traits a character has is up to the
character’s training in a specific endeavour; each is rated 0       player—two or three salient ones is a good start. A
to 100 or higher by a Mastery Level (ML). While Attributes          select few can often more clearly describe a character
influence a skill’s score (and cap its ultimate development),       than a lengthy and perhaps muddled litany.
sheer time and effort from training also affect mastery.
Standing: a character’s money and possessions reflect both
Family (inheritance) and Persona (occupation).
Mysteries: characters have the chance to shape their own
destiny through the expression of the three Mysteries. It is
especially glimpsed through astrological fate.

Attribute Descriptions
The following two pages display the six physical and six
mental Attributes.
Physical Attributes: Strength (STR), Endurance (END),
Dexterity (DEX), Agility (AGL), Perception (PER),
Comeliness (CML).
Mental Attributes: Aura (AUR), Will (WIL), Reasoning
(REA), Creativity (CRE), Empathy (EMP), Eloquence (ELO).
A table for each one provides trait-like descriptions for the
entire range of scores. These are a guide to how folk in the
game world might describe the given attribute: a character
with Agility 18 might be called graceful.
   Attributes directly affect the Mastery Level (ML) of
a skill—the average of two equals its Skill Base (SB), as
further explained on page 45. Attributes may also be tested
individually themselves with a d100 roll versus their score
times five.
   Generating attribute scores and other characteristics
begins on page 38 (step 10).

Skill assignment is done through Development Points (DP). When one
DP is allocated to a skill, its current SM increases by one. Adding one
point to Melee SM2 raises it to SM3; adding one point to Metalcraft SM0
raises it to SM1. The maximum SM allowed is 5, after which each DP
improves skills by way of Mastery Boosts (page 47 sidebar).
   Follow the stages listed in the sidebar above right to assign a
character’s skill DP. The Nolora: Skills highlighted section on page 50
provides a complete example of skill assignment.

[�] Folk Skills
Since many Elder Folk have lifespans far greater than humans, and
usually spend many decades in adolescence, they develop more
automatic skills than humans do. See the sidebar for such Folk Skills
granted to Kuzhai and Sinai characters.

mastery levels
After stage 8 (Sunsign Skills), compute the Mastery Level (ML) of every
skill. Characters also have an ML in the skills listed on the Skills List
table that have an SM of one or more—even if no DP were spent on them.
These automatic skills are already shown on the character sheet; every
character gains them to at least the listed SM level, if not at a higher SM
through development.
Attributes: the twelve Attributes each have a Mastery Level (ML) equal
to its generated score multiplied by five (ATT × 5). A STR12 has ML60, for
instance. An Attribute ML can be tested with a d100 roll just like a Skill
ML—see pages 60–62.
The section on the next page explains the eight stages of Nolora’s Skill
Development, including the calculations of Mastery Levels. Character
generation continues with step 13 in the Standing section on page 51.

         few paces behind the cart, Alun walks
         at the edge of the track, not always careful
         to avoid a sudden slip into the wheel-cut
ruts of the hardened mud. Kora could never tell if
her brother was tired or bored or sad—probably
sad. On foot herself, leading in front, she turns to
click assurance to Ota, their draught horse, and
tries to get a look at Alun’s eyes. But he is looking
down, frowning, as he trudges along with his
cloak wrapped tightly around his arms.
   The tall hedgerows on either side of the road
mean they are nearing Lasomer, now passing
through its peripheral fields. Before turning away
from Alun, Kora spots, beyond the hedges, two
farmers in the distant field abruptly abandoning
their ox-driven plough. A third briefly stays
behind, trying to unhitch it, but soon flees
himself. They run in the same direction as she and
Alun, at a closing angle, stumbling now and again
as they dart over the earthen ridges in the field.
   Kora looks down the track ahead. The smell of
smoke reaches her before she sees it—a belching
plume that rises above the treeline. To her left,
a woman in the distinct green spring robes of a
Peonian priestess suddenly appears through a
gate in the hedge. With trembling hands raised to
her face, she blurts out in a sobbing panic ‘They’re
back!’, then spins around and runs.
   Kora stops Ota and goes to the back of the cart.
She sets a stack of pots on the ground, hauls out a
long blanketed bundle, and removes from it a war
sword; her grip easily turns its heavy blade. Alun
looks at her emptily, opens his cloak, and draws
out a bowstring he keeps coiled up a sleeve.

Lore                                                                                                                                                        Physical
Lore skills reflect mundane knowledge. While Craft, Nature,                                      While Physical Attributes describe a character’s innate
and Esoteric skills also require erudition, the various Lore                                   physique, Physical Group skills test actions related to the
skills specifically measure the grasp of Kethiran technology,                              body or senses. Physical skills usually do not require training,
history, and culture. Aside from Cookery, Folklore, one Ritual                                     except for highly specialised feats like Acrobatics and
skill, and Physician, Lore skills require training.                                                                                          Legerdemain.

Social                                                                                                                                                       Combat
These skills measure how well one influences other                                                          Fighting includes raw attributes and skills from
people. Largely based upon eloquence, they also                                                          other groups—Strength, Command—but Combat
feature perceptive powers, creativity, and physical                                                        skills measure effective action amid the chaos of
beauty. Apart from foreign languages, characters                                                         battle. Everyone can muster some ability to defend
may test Social skills without training.                                                                         themselves; true prowess requires training.

Nature                                                                                                                                                            Craft
Nature Group skills measure wilderness lore. They usually                                  Skills that produce mundane technologies, items, or effects
demand keen senses, wit, or raw determination. Outdoor                                     belong to the Craft Group. Something is made in the world:
knowledge is hard-earned—the untrained character may                                     jewellery, a weapon, music. Craft skills rely on the senses and
intuitively attempt only the simplest of survival tasks.                               dexterity or even strength, and almost always requires training.

                                                                       Esoterica
The skills that deal with the arcane or astral mysteries comprise the Esoterica group. They do not receive Sunsign Modifiers like those of
the six mundane skill groups. Instead, a character’s birth sunsign influences each esoteric skill uniquely and more directly. While briefly
        described in the skill entries, esoteric skills receive full explanation in their respective section of Chapter 6: The Mysteries.

animalcraft
The practice of domesticating, breeding, caring for, and
handling animals, which includes droving and driving
carts and wagons. While in practice some occupations
focus on one type of creature, the Animalcraft skill applies
to all domesticated animals within a given culture. In
northwest Venarive, this includes four principal groups:
birds, dogs, horses, and livestock. Livestock include sheep,
goats, oxen, cows, pigs, chickens, ducks, and geese.
   Players can expand the above list to include other
groups, such as camels, cats, and apes.

animal lore
A character may test Animalcraft to glean information
about a domesticated animal’s health or demeanour.

     Hartbows: when making a bow, an Ælrhin crafter

     3. A successful SR infuses the bow with an intangible
     faeriecraft quality (page 93) that halves its draw. This is not
     an arcane enchantment but rather an astral expression of
     the Ælrhin crafter’s soul. Thus, magic dispelling has no
     effect.

application: how the potion takes effect. Most are ingested (some as smoke);
others are applied to the skin as a poultice . When a paste is adhered to a blade
or broadhead projectile, the potion only takes effect when the weapon’s edge or
point aspect impact achieves a non-Glancing Blow injuring strike.
effect: what the potion does. Longevity is the time increment for the potency to
stage down one level after application (Great to Strong; Strong to Mild; and Mild
to no effect). Thus, applied Great potions last one increment at each potency.
 m s g : herbal potency (Mild, Strong, or Great). An SV Test refers to the
preparation Herblore test in step 2 (page 74). Some refer to Healing Rate (HR); or
Shock State, such as incapacitation (INC) or unconsciousness (UNC).

Quicklime Pot (Ceramic Pot, 2 qt): limestone cooked into
calcium oxide; the broken pot explodes into a powdery
10-foot diameter caustic cloud of lime. Usually hurled by
a small siege engine, the large pot could also be lobbed
short distances by hand. Targets within the cloud are
incapacitated (INC) from choking and blindness (Shock
Reroll 2d3 rounds later; page 169).
Take the following steps to fashion a mixture:
[�] Time: one day to prepare either type, in quantities
essentially capped only by the budget. Fire Pots cost 12d to
make; Quicklime Pots cost 24d.
[�] Test: make a Mineralogy Success Value test.
[�] Result: the SV itself serves as a d10 Target Number for
when the pot is later actually used (see step 5).
[�] Duration: once prepared, such mixtures have an
indefinite duration, although certain conditions might
ruin or set them off. A successful d10 roll against the TN
avoids such triggers.
[�] Application: when thrown or hurled, make a d10
roll against the TN. Failure means a Fire Pot does
only d4 + 2 Fire impact; or a Quicklime Pot allows
Shock Reroll d3 rounds later. Pots fashioned from a CF
SV test in step 2 are, instead, duds if this d10 roll fails.

runecraft
The interpretation of Fate (divination) as manifested in the
casting of runestones, a technique native to the Kuzhai and
Ivinians. See Chapter 6: the Mysteries (page 281).


script per Script
A character’s ability to scribe and read a given writing
system. Languages may lack written form or may be
represented in one or more systems; and the same script
might be used for several languages. To read a language,
one must have both the relevant Language and Script skills
(see the complete list for Venarive in Appendix ii).
Retests: tasks may be retested for the same work only after
Script (scribing) or Language (reading) increases by 10 ML.

scribing
Characters measure notation legibility with a Script
(Language · Drawing) Success Value test. For copying an
extant work, a Drawing SV test (−2 SV) is a second option.
Dictation: a scribe receiving dictation from the work’s
author has −20 penalty to the Script test.

survival
Wilderness lore, especially with respect to travelling,
procuring shelter, and living off the land. This includes the
knowledge of wild animals, their traits and their habitats.
Many vocations develop Survival skill, but anyone can
apply a little common sense and attempt it untrained at
SM1. The Trekking Routine in Chapter 5: Adventure
covers most uses of the Survival skill. Consider also:

hunting
Pursuing and killing animals for sport or sustenance is
not its own skill but rather a task utilising the Survival,
Tracking, and missile weapon skills. Simply use the
Trekking Routine to resolve the hunter’s stalking and the
Missile or Melee Sequence to resolve the attack. These
sample game produce the following number of food-days:

 Lion             20 + 2d6         Wolf            15 + 1d10

wooden structures
Making wooden edifices first requires a Design Roll of the
Engineering skill (page 70), followed by a Construction
Roll. Use the same procedure for the number of workers
as explained in the Masonry entry (page 78), but substitute
the given skill below for the test. Small cottages, fences,
hovels, and palisades do not require a Design Roll.

chapter 4

Possessions
      was told the ring would be in the small
      wooden box sitting on the table next to Lady
      Alawyn’s bed. With the sun dropping close to
the western ridge, the hallway in the keep outside
her bedroom is already quite dark. I stand to the
side of the door, clutching three thick candles,
waiting to place them inside for the maid to light
soon. This only gives me several minutes.
    Lady Alawyn and her cousin come out of the
room, her darting eyes registering the candles.
‘It’s quite frightful—I don’t think she made it out
of Waleden in time,’ she remarks as they turn and
stride slowly down the hall. Gowns had lengthened
over the past few years to drag now across the
floor, and the two had perfected the slow and
awkward stride needed to raise the embroidered
hems slightly with their feet and knees to avoid
tripping. To do so with the grace of appearing not
to try requires practice.
    I wait respectfully until they descend, one
careful step at a time, the stairs at the end of the
hallway. I then enter the bedchamber, its door left
open, and go to the box on the side table. The lid
displays a stag head inlay—this is the one—so I
open it. As if forgotten, the black onyx ring lies
buried under a mound of broaches and chains.
As I grab the ring, I’m immediately startled by
the clap of cantering hooves striking the stone
courtyard outside. Hurrying over to the narrow
aperture, I see down below a half dozen armoured
men-at-arms in yellow surcoats, their horses spent
from a hard ride. Several have already dismounted
and are rushing the front door.
    It’s time for me to leave.

to-hand fighting, throwing, and projecting missiles.
Despite having a variety of traits, all weapons share two

                       axes
Battleaxe [chivalric]
(Long axe · Greataxe) Derived from the wood axe, the battleaxe
concentrates its weight in the heavy blade, increasing impact but
making it slower in handling. Wielding it one-handed increases reach
(lng 6), but only the strongest may do so accurately.

                                   strike mode example
The poleaxe is a versatile weapon and serves as a good example of how to note Strike
Modes. Here are several ways a character with STR14 may wield a poleaxe two-handed:

 poleaxe strike modes                      hft   lng             zd    imp             imp ta other traits
 1: 		 swung axe-head, 2-h                 13    6               d6   d8 + 9e           6e    defence −10
 2: 		 swung hammer-head, 2-h              13    6               d6   d6+ 7b            3b    defence −10
 3: 		 thrusted spear-point, 2-h           13    6t              d8   d8 + 6p           4p
 4: 		 swung shaft, 2-h                    13    4               d6   d6+ 3b            3b    melee −5

Some players may wish to note beforehand all the possible modes for a weapon,
especially for those as variable as a poleaxe. However, for most weapons, such record
keeping can usually wait until the pertinent situation arises in the game.
Weapon Options: GMs may apply weapon modes and traits in novel ways to address
unique situations.  For instance, thrusting with the butt end of a staff could be treated as
half-swording that instead inflicts d6 + 0b impact; or a staff wielded to trip a target uses
the polearm’s Length (LNG) in the Trip attack (page 106) instead of an unarmed LNG2.

Battlesword [chivalric]

Broadsword [chivalric]
(Arming sword • War sword) The most popular weapon of the feudal gentry, the
broadsword allows for a high degree of control. This is a lethal advantage against all
defences but mail and plate, which routinely turn its slicing blows.
 wq hft lng           zd     impact traits                                   lb price
  12    10      5      d6    d10 + 3e thrust d8 + 1p                          3     156d


Estoc [chivalric]
Designed to penetrate gaps in plate and mail, the estoc allows half-swording (page
102) more safely since only its tip is sharp. Its thrust-only style makes wielding it
one-handed more difficult than a swung broadsword of similar weight. The thin
blade sometimes overpenetrates, missing vital organs that the thicker points of
spears and other swords would not.
 wq hft lng           zd     impact traits                                   lb price
  12    14     5t      d6     d8 + 3p ar 1p (2-handed) • impact ta 3p 3            168d


Falchion [chivalric]
The design of the falchion’s blade calls for chopping strikes. It shares elements of a
sword’s control, but with its weight centred further out on the blade, the falchion
imparts a higher effective heft than a broadsword of similar weight.
 wq hft lng           zd     impact traits                                   lb price
  12    12      4      d6     d8 + 4e impact ta 6e                            3    120d


Scimitar [simple]
While less routinely penetrative than the broadsword, the scimitar’s curved
blade enhances the slashing injuries produced from its strikes that do land
well. Its tip is usually not extremely sharp.

Shortsword [simple]
(Sword) Carried by many common folk, the shortsword primarily calls for
cutting strikes. Its shorter length turns to an advantage in tight quarters against
foes wielding spears and longer swords.

Composite Crossbow [simple]
  (Siege crossbow) With a string as thick as a thumb and a composite wood and

  spanner. For this reason many are relegated to siege defence, where the shooters
  can more easily gain shelter during the time-consuming reloading.

      Structures
      Architecture varies according to culture and climate.
      The following entries describe the various buildings and
      fortifications listed in the Standing table (page 52),
      applying mostly to the styles of northwestern Venarive.
      Local Maps produced by Kelestia Productions, such as the
      portion of Burzyn in the Kingdom of Chybisa shown to the
      right, use a scale of 1 mm to 10 feet. The white buildings
      represent all manner of wattle and daub, wooden, and
      stone structures, with prominent stone edifices such as
      castles and walls shaded black. The buildings are kept a
      blank white to ease identification and to enable clear player
      notation and modification.

chapter 5

        alios purposefully folds his hands
        across the short stack of tattered vellum
        on the table before him, a subtle gesture
of defiance to the negotiation. Ulven, master of
Scholars’ Hall, shifts uneasily in an opposing chair,
worried the chance to acquire the ancient Jarind
documents is slipping away. He glances at Kalios’
implacable grey eyes, idly taps the table, and
considers a different tack.



The Emhlen warden Lerelyn marches sombrely
along the mountain trail to Abrelyn, the pilgrims
she leads nervously attentive to her watchfulness,
unable to forget the previous night’s horror. The
bright sunshine fails to distract them from the
encroaching shadow beneath the trees. Erynos,
senior among the devotees, encourages them:
‘Come, we must go quickly!’



On a clear day in the High Vale of Our Mothers,
Kath hunters can usually see the dark line of the
Kald river far to the east. Today, however, with
thick fog still clinging stubbornly all around, Loxa
can barely make out the near shore of Eagle Pond
two hundred paces away. How strange to fret
about it now, he muses, choking on rising blood
and slumping to the wet grass. He doesn’t even feel
the arrow shaft buried in his chest snap off, now
only half-conscious of mail-clad figures emerging
from the mist.

      Gateways
      A gateway is a type of energy force that transfers an entity
      from one point in the physical world to another point.
      For beings, it is thought that gateways transport the
      Aura-connection to the body, removing the anchor at the
      starting point and then instantaneously reforming it at the
      destination, where the body reappears. Two gateway types
      known to folklore are Barasi Points and Godstones.

      Barási Points
      Named after the mage who studied them centuries ago,
      Barasi Points link naturally occurring channels between
      worlds. He described three types of such ‘filaments’:

combat
Adventures in the world of Kethira can lead to combat.
Political conflict might involve assassination, border
raids, and the outright invasion of kingdoms and realms.
                                                               Melee
Overland travel in many places includes the menace of          The melee rules make personal armed conflict quite
brigands and roving bands of mercenaries. Sea and river        consequential. Injuries accrue realistically—a single well-
voyages risk piracy and wreckers. Most dangerously,            aimed blow can suddenly incapacitate a character, and
exploration into the world’s remote corners often exposes      those who die usually do so from bleeding. While cinema
characters to strange beasts and esoteric horror.              and fiction seem to exaggerate depictions of bravery, it is
                                                               a simple fact that some folk perform quite exceptionally in
roleplaying combat                                             response to violent threat. Fighting spirit alone very often
When resolving combat, the GM vividly describes the            distinguishes the victorious from the vanquished.
environment of the battle, and the players report their
character’s actions within it. The open-ended Star
approach to skill tests allows characters to perform special
                                                               melee routine
feats as spontaneously chosen by the players. Instead          The Melee Routine most easily resolves small conflicts
of narrowly defined combat abilities (‘Mighty Blow’), the      between up to about ten individuals. While it is called
flexible system itself manifests the character’s unique        ‘melee’, the routine covers missiles, mounts, and esoteric
attacks and manoeuvres as narrated by the players.             actions. Morale also plays an important role.
                                                                  One melee round represents about five seconds in the
maps & miniatures                                              world. During each round, every character receives a turn.
Combats can be fought without the use of a formal              The GM and players may wish to narrate a character’s
map, especially those conflicts involving just a couple        action first and use the rules to express this description
of participants. However, the rules also readily lend          second. The game sequence should help manifest the
themselves to hobby miniatures and game boards.                unfolding drama rather than ploddingly constrain it.
                                                                  The GM’s first task is to establish and recount for
                                                               the players the melee’s environment. How far away are
                                                               combatants? What is the terrain? Are there any special
                                                               details that might affect actions, such as rain or darkness?
                                                               After this general nature is established, the melee proceeds
                                                               in rounds consisting of these five steps:
                                                               [�] Alertness...................................................page ���
                                                               [�] Initiative...................................................page ���
                                                               [�] Engagement..............................................page ���
                                                               [�] Actions.....................................................page ���
                                                               [�] Morale......................................................page ���

                                                               Scale: one round lasts five seconds. Distances are
                                                               measured in feet but often referred to in five-foot
                                                               increments called spaces. Groups using game maps can
                                                               represent a space according to their preference—a hex, a
                                                               square, or even an inch on tabletop terrain.

                                                               encounter distance
                                                               The surrounding environment likely dictates how close
                                                               opponents are at the start of combat. Skulking in the
                                                               shadow of an alley puts characters within literal striking
                                                               distance of passing targets; attacking a camp amid a sparse
                                                               forest leaves a longer approach. For help establishing this
                                                               distance, GMs can refer to the Awareness Distance table
                                                               (page 150).

trauma
In addition to social interactions, travel, and combat,
characters will likely face physical and mental trauma
                                                                             Mental Trauma
during their adventures. Most physical trauma affects the                    Often as debilitating as bodily damage, mental trauma
body, and most mental trauma, the mind. Some instances                       manifests in three ways:
can damage both.                                                             Fear: a reaction to perceived danger, most commonly
                                                                             arising from the threat of violence. Characters rely
Physical Trauma                                                              on will, reasoning, and experience to withstand fear,
Perhaps the more common of the two types, physical                           whether responding to the stress of combat or resisting
trauma is divided into three categories:                                     intimidation. Fear usually comes and goes quickly.
                                                                                Certain strange sources of fear affect folk more
Fatigue: an overall lack of energy that can result from                      intensely. Characters might face such aberrance from
arduous travel, lengthy battles, and spellcasting. Such                      ghosts or bizarre beasts.
exhaustion accumulates as fatigue, a penalty applied to
almost all tests. It usually subsides with rest and sleep, but               Stress: a longer-lasting response to severe trauma. The
weakness fatigue can last throughout lingering ailments.                     mental equivalent of physical injury, such stress can leave
                                                                             a character’s psyche altered, sometimes permanently. The
Injury: direct and more life-threatening damage to the                       most frightening type of stress—the dreaded Shadow of
body. Injuries manifest as specific states and effects,                      Bukrai—can even rend a character’s soul.
including bleeding, shock, and impairment.
                                                                             Aural Shock: the temporary disruption of the character’s
Ailments: physical trauma other than fatigue and injury.                     connection to the spirit world. While not permanent, Aural
This includes disease, malnutrition, poison, and conditions                  Shock prevents Esoteric Group skill and Aura tests.
such as heat exhaustion and cold exposure.

Mental Trauma                                                                         types of fear
                                                                                      The Reaction and Morale Rolls of combat
In addition to suffering physical trauma during adventures, characters                are types of fear mental trauma. However,
might also face mental trauma such as fear, stress, and aural shock.                  the psychophysiology of confronting violent
                                                                                      threat—especially that deriving from folk—

fear 		
                                                                                      differs slightly from other sources of fear.
                                                                                      Trained warriors respond more successfully in
Simple fear is not uncommon; it arises and subsides rather quickly.                   these situations, and so Reaction and Morale
                                                                                      rolls test Initiative rather than Will.
Experiencing intimidation, suffering spell effects, or confronting a
ghost can all force characters to make a Fear Roll. When required, they
test Will on the Fear Roll table and apply the results immediately.                   aberrance example

psy: the last column indicates whether the character accrues Psyche Stress
Levels and how many. The amount is 0, 1 (CF5), or 2 (CF0), but facing entities with
Aberrance increases the accrued PSY level by the indicated ABE amounts.


Aberrance
Some sources of fear are so bizarre, grotesque, or deviant that they make
resisting fear more difficult and failing to do so more consequential.
The source is usually a freakish beast or spirit (purely psychological), but
could also be a fell artefact or spell.
   Whatever the source, it expresses Aberrance (ABE), a score with no
technical limit but usually between 1 and 6. Chapter 7: Bestiary notes
which entities have Aberrance and how much.

aberrance effect
The moment they perceive a source of Aberrance, characters and
creatures make a Fear Roll. The GM determines when such ‘perception’
takes place and applies. Entities who possess Aberrance themselves are
usually immune to its effect from other sources (see Advice & Options
on page 401 of Chapter 7: Bestiary for more discussion).
Fear Penalty: all accompanying Will tests have a penalty equal to the
source’s ABE ×5. This penalty also applies to the victim’s Initiative tests.
Psyche Stress: Aberrance increases the Psyche Stress Levels accrued
from the Will test on the Fear Roll table. On a failed test, the amount is
increased by the ABE score (see sidebar example). Even on a Success (S),
victims accrue PSY equal to half the ABE score, rounded down.

chapter 6

The Mysteries
         elestia is the cosmic all—everything
         that exists, the sum total of all realities
         within and beyond space and time. The
most profound traditions developed by the various
peoples of Kethira to understand Kelestia are
collectively called the Mysteries. Scholars often
distinguish between three branches: the Arcane,
the Astral, and the Divine.


   The Arcane Mysteries attempt to draw
directly from the primal forces of Kelestia. Its
practitioners train themselves to interact closely
with these energies, and their personal skill
greatly shapes how they manifest them in the
physical world. This is what most call magic.


   The Astral Mysteries also require skill to
explore. However, the journey takes students
into the unseen spirit world. While their training
affects the success of reaching such an ethereal
place, astralists gain power only through
beseeching, once there, great spirit entities. If
successful, they return able to express subtle
esoteric power in the physical world.


   The Divine Mysteries involve neither the
active control of magic nor the petitioning of
mighty spirits. Instead, their power results from
supra-normal entities (gods) acting in the world
through a chosen mortal, whose connection to any
resulting blessing or miracle is unfathomable.

      Odívshè             1-rd   2-rd   2-rd   3-rd   3-rd   4-rd

    Ultimately, spell invention is game-art, not
    game-science. Players should know well the
    over 200 spells already provided and balance
    new effects to the established ones. While they
    have a listed maximum Complexity Level of VI,
    there is likely no theoretical limit. It is thought
    that Grey Mages over the centuries, either
    alone or more likely in consort, have at least
    attempted research into more powerful magic.

Alchemy
Alchemy shares with the other Pvaric Arcane Mysteries          Example: a hunter trekking through a forest might forage for a
the study of ethereal energy. This spectrum includes           plant or herb to use in making a salve to treat the burn injuries

and Water, and the various other principles categorised        requires a Success Value test of Herblore to craft (page 74).
as Neutral. Whereas incanters such as Pvarists directly            Exotic concoctions made primarily from minerals are called
channel the principles to cast spells, an alchemist            mixtures but are still treated similarly to potions. The substance
manipulates them from a distance, guiding the energies         known as quicklime is an example (page 81).

complicated and time-consuming processes, alchemists           esoteric concoctions

and minerals in order to produce various elixirs, each of      arcane manipulation of the elemental principles found

Concoctions
There are three types of concoctions, the distinction
between which helps define the alchemical process.

mundane concoctions
Several occupations incorporate herbs and minerals into
the substances they make or services they perform—
lexigrapher (pigments), perfumer (aromatic
flowers), glassworker (soda ash), embalmer
(preservatives), mason (limestone). However, this
incorporation is not alchemy, but rather, in game
terms, simply a part of the occupational skill itself.
Example: although a perfumer might utilise various
herbs and minerals, crafting perfume is simply a Success
Value test of Perfumery skill. The necessary ingredients
are usually purchased from an apothecary and then
incorporated into the fragrance.

exotic concoctions
Certain rarer concoctions, called potions and mixtures,
require a Success Value test of Herblore (page 74) or
Mineralogy (page 81), respectively. Again, such work
is not alchemy—not magical—because it does not
require the manipulation of the elemental principles.
The ingredients used in potions and mixtures are
either much rarer or more volatile or complicated to
deal with than those found in mundane concoctions.
While ‘mundane’ themselves, exotic concoctions have
unique game effects, such as poison or quicklime. Most
of what traditional or tribal shamans and physicians
create are these exotic concoctions.

                                                                                                                       divination




Divination
Like other arcanists, most diviners throughout Lythia
understand magic forces Pvarically, according to the
spectrum of elemental principles anchored by Earth,
Metal, Fire, Air, Aura, and Water. Among the three
arcane mysteries, divination interacts the least
directly with the principles, and so its magic
manifests the most subtly. Whereas the incanter
directly channels ethereal energies to cast spells
or invoke talents, and the alchemist obliquely
manipulates them to create elixirs, the diviner
merely observes them.
   Diviners interpret the principles in order to
make statements about the future. The three
methods detailed in this section are Astrology,
Runecraft, and Tarotry, although others exist
throughout Kethira’s many cultures. The arcane
talents of Clairvoyance, Psychometry, and
Visnomy are not divination, as their power
concerns the present or past (likewise for the
Savoryan spells Enquiry and Wisdom). However,
the Prescience talent is the divinatory equivalent
of Natural Attunement—an innate arcane ability to
observe the future. Many revered ‘oracles’ throughout
the world likely render their visions with Prescience.
Whatever the method, all divination functions with a clear
distinction between destiny and fate.                         rules for Fate Points manifest just exactly that, enabling
                                                              players to control their character’s destiny through their

   The Sunsign Wheel displays the twelve sunsigns on the outer rim in line with their corresponding Pvaric elements (convocations). Thus, the first sunsign
   of the year (I Ulandus) is positioned in the lower left, in line with Fyvria; the others appear counterclockwise from here, up to the top and down to the last
  sunsign of the year (XII Lado), corresponding with Odivshe. Astrological tables, such as on the following page, list sunsigns in order of their position in the
                         Tuzyn Reckoning calendar, starting with Ulandus (first row/new year) through Lado (last row/end of year).

                                                                             what first distinguished Khruni from Runic.

                                                                             Similarly to the suggestion given about

The shaman is an occupation prevalent among most tribal         The Priest is often a role filled by a shaman or sorcerer—
societies on Kethira. Its practitioners develop techniques      traditions vary as to the presence and extent of the Ritual
to undertake astral journeys, during which they beseech         skill. However, the role of ‘shaman’ in some tribes might be
spirit entities and immerse with primal forces to grant         subsumed in a more prominent priestly figure.
them esoteric powers. While a given shaman might also           The Stranger could start out as an outsider but, through
practice magic through Natural Attunement and, even             exceptional talent and many years of deep acceptance,
more likely, administer the tribe’s religious practices         could rise to fill the tradition’s role of shaman.
through Ritual skill, shamanism itself is an astral mystery

and thus distinct from both the arcane and divine.
   The call to be a shaman often comes from lucid dreams
or a near-death experience in childhood. It may also grow       From whatever the tradition and archetype, a shaman
directly from the Disembodiment talent or stem from a           must be able to lift the veil that separates the spirit world

force remains unique to tribal peoples, who rarely teach the    Guides, to perform Rites, and to bestow Talismans.
mystery to even worthy strangers.

Tradition
Each tribe practicing shamanism has its own tradition.
Such traditions function not unlike the convocations for
the Shek-Pvar, uniquely highlighting and limiting certain
aspects of the Mystery. An overview of six tribal shamanic
traditions found in Venarive is given on page 301.
   Characters who are not native to a specific tribal society
are considered outsiders to its tradition. They are limited
even as targets in receiving shamanistic effects.
Folklore: an outsider with high Folklore might have
knowledge of a tribe, but this does not equate to practicing
its tradition. This requires years of direct contact even
possibly to gain such acceptance.

Shamanic Archetypes
Shaman is a social role made possible by membership
in a tribal tradition. While the word ‘shaman’ is used
throughout the rules, it can apply to several archetypes:
The Shaman is skilled in Trance, whether through
meditation, chant, dance, or some other method. Such
characters usually have the Shaman occupation, but
they might have also developed the Trance skill while
performing other roles, such as tribal chieftain.
The Sorcerer reaches the spirit world through arcane
means. This is usually done with the Disembodiment
arcane talent, or by way of Natural Attunement in the
Lyahvi convocation and training in the Figure spell.

    itself, when followers perform it along
    with Communion on the 30th of the
    month, they increase their blessing
    bonus—and its possible maximum—
    by 1. The faithful enjoy an increased
    clarity and vivacity to their dreams.

    Summoning
    In Pvaric spellcasting, the mage creates a Form
    and then fills it with Principle, the channelled
    ethereal energy that triggers the spell effect.
    The model for Summoning is different.
    Here, summoners carefully formulate their
    request and then harness Gateway forces to
    transmit the message to the desired entity
    in the astralscape, who still might deny the
    summons.
        Priests follow four steps to attempt ritual
    summoning.

         he aperagris, master of the High
         Discipline, clutches with his left hand the
         chain around the waist of a wretched man
 who teeters at the edge of the octagonal pit. The
 grip prevents the captive from plunging into its
 blackened depths, but the gouts of infernal heat
 rushing up have blistered and scorched his face
 and bare chest. One arm hangs limply, broken
 and twisted backwards at the elbow, and blood
 streams from torturing cuts to his throat. The
 Aperagris raises a steel mace in his other hand
 and shouts in Surikal ‘Release!’, and so he does—
 and the chained man falls headlong into the pit,
 not conscious enough to scream.
   From the circle of swaying priests around
the edge of the chamber, a high priest—the
Viriahn—now strides forward and begins a loud
and discordant chant in the ancient tongue
Zakimladal. He stops at the pit, and bellows a
tearful and angry exhortation for many minutes.
Sweat pours from beneath his lacquered helm, but
the scales of ornate armour deflect the heat.
   A wispy smoke appears in the pit and slowly
rises in strange curls. It gradually collects into a
thick mass, stretching to the room’s stone ceiling
in defiance of the scant breeze. Within its inky
centre two small red spots materialise—two eyes,
then clearly the fiery visage of a creature made
of hardened magma. It appears suspended in
the black smoke, with two scalloped wings slowly
flapping, keeping it bizarrely afloat. After a final
hoarse shout, the Viriahn collapses to hands and
knees, and a second cloven-hoofed beast appears,
awaiting command alongside the first.

A being is a living entity with a soul in the spirit world that
is anchored to a natural body in the physical world. Beings

present
Even after seven thousand years, the
kingdoms of Azadmere on Hârn and
Kuzjera in Ivinia have remained in contact
with each other; they are also the most
widely known by human society. These
Kuzhai are aware of both Erdar and
Larhakul in western Katarh but have
seemingly lost contact with them.
    Only Kuzhan scholars know the exact
location of Merdain, the first city, its
status clouded by rumours of corruption.
The realm of Kazerad in far-off Kamerand
is nearly legend even in the minds of
Kuzhai. It remains isolated within a
land struggling against the cruelty of the
Empire of Yerazhen.
    Lastly, the location of Zhumertol,
founded by the tribe of Tol, is lost even to
the Kuzhan wise, whose memories shape
it as a utopia of peace and plenty.

 1   flight
The air is a dragon’s most natural, physical
world habitat. In flight it observes potential
meals and possible invaders. Being aloft also
gives it ample opportunity to invoke arcane
talents (step 2).
• Although dragons can make terrifying
  double Move plunges, they tend to
  soar at a full Move in order still
  to express their breath
  weapon.
• A dragon in flight
  would likely only land
  after a successful
  use of its breath
  weapon, when targets seem
  sufficiently ‘softened’.

2    arcane talents
Since it invokes as a free action, a dragon
with arcane talents uses them often,
hesitating only after gaining 10 or more
fatigue.    
• It usually starts with Fiery/Chilling Visage.
• In its lair, the dragon masks itself with
  Ethereal Smoke/Darkness, or Stillness.
• In the wilderness, it overcomes prey with
  Exhausting, Gloom Wave, or Speed Burst.
• In melee at the start of its turn, the dragon
  always targets a foe with Enthral.

spirit world and has no inherent body in the physical
world. Many spirits, such as ghosts, remain forever                   While all spirits are naturally incorporeal, some of them

world. They appear as bipedal humanoids
with cloven hooves, scalloped wings,
and deadly claws. They have a black,
squamous hide, as if hardened like cold
magma. Literally shrouded in shadow and
fire, all V’hiri wield weapons favoured by
their master—metal-barbed whips, heavy
maces, and sickle-shaped swords. While
in single battle mortal folk can sometimes
defeat members of the weaker orders, the
eight Sons exude a fell power insuperable
to all but the mightiest Kethiran.
Blood of Agrik: V’hiri have blood akin to
oozing magma, and they can suffer Shock
from bleeding. V’hir blood that touches a
creature inflicts the demon’s Fire impact
(see V’hir Abilities table, next page).
Flame: V’hir bodies and weapons are
enveloped in dancing flame. A successful
weapon attack inflicts the listed Fire
impact to the very same location struck,
rolled separately as its own burn injury.
Bonus Impact TA apply only to the
weapon aspect’s impact. Burn injuries
do not compound with weapon aspect
injuries—but both can compound with
themselves over successive strikes.
   Opponents who are victorious with an
unarmed attack or defence against a V’hir
also suffer its fire impact to the zone they
used in the test (in a random location).

chapter 8

Campaign
         bris takes one last look at the
         valley behind him. On this clear spring
         morning, he can still see the main hall and
outbuildings of Belveron, the manor his father
manages as bailiff for Duke Anavras at Neoma.
The rich meadowlands that stretch out from it
along the banks of the Legama river have provided
ample livelihood to generations of herders. Today
he spots a handful of the largest flocks of sheep
meandering about during their early grazing.
   He turns to catch up with the two people his
father charged him with escorting—Elban, an
affable scholar from far-off Hârn, and Nolora, a
taciturn guide and member of the tribal Emhle
from the surrounding mountains. They have come
to interview Maken, the elderly herder who said
he lost sheep to a marauding beast. He claims to
have witnessed it flying off with a ewe, or at least a
large part of its remains.
   Obris reaches them at the familiar hill crest
lined with the crumbling low wall of a ruined
watchtower. ‘I say!’ Elban exclaims, his interest
piqued by a small rock cairn piled next to the wall.
Just as Obris begins to share the story behind the
ancient ruins, he stops suddenly, noticing Nolora
further up standing motionless on a small boulder,
with a hand thrust in the air to halt them.
   She seems to peer into the forest ahead, but is
actually listening, intently. To the sudden silence.
Obris instinctively grabs the pommel of his sword
and a nerve twitches at the back of his neck. With
dread, he’s compelled to turn around. Across the
expansive and quiet valley, near Mount Himlenkul
miles away, he swears he can make out wings.
8 campaign
  game elements




   Game Elements
   Most participants enjoy playing HârnMaster over several
   gaming sessions, with the PCs facing a series of narratively
   related challenges that enable them to explore the setting
   more widely. These longer games are called campaigns, and
   they consist of three broad elements—adventures, non-
   player characters (NPCs), and character development. Even
   shorter, single-session games involve the first two.
   Adventures (page 406): an adventure involves the PCs
   facing one or more separate challenges called encounters. A
   campaign consists of two or more sequential adventures.
   Non-Player Characters (page 410): the people and creatures
   the PCs meet during an encounter are called non-player
   characters (NPC). The GM usually controls their actions.
   Character Development (page 413): over the course of
   several adventures, PCs may improve skills, accumulate
   possessions, and modify their social influence.

   Kèthîran Campaigns
   GMs and players should consider the following five key
   traits about both the canon setting of Kethira and the
   system of HârnMaster. While published materials reflect
   these characteristics, advice is given for how gamers can
   modify each of them for campaigns of their own liking.

   culture
   The technology, demographics, and societies of Kethira
   closely reflect many medieval Terran cultures of the 9th to
   14th centuries. While not perfectly analogous in details,

To generate occupational status, characters make a Success Value
test in their occupation’s primary skill. If this primacy is not obvious in
the given Occupation subtable (pages 42–44), the GM designates this
skill. Next, further modify this SV by the result of an Intrigue test: −2
SV (CF); −1 SV (F); 0 SV (S); +1 SV (CS).
    Locate the resulting Success Value (SV) in the following
table (above right). The character has the corresponding
occupational status, treated similarly to family Estrangement
(page 34). A precise ‘ML’ could be derived from this SV in
order to allow Occupation Rolls similar to Kinship Rolls.
